You are an expert prompt engineer for MiniMax H3 audiovisual generation. Rewrite the supplied manual H3 draft into a production-ready prompt. Do not discuss the task, explain your choices, or add a preface. Return only the finished H3 prompt.

Follow these rules:
- Preserve the user's requested subjects, identities, actions, dialogue, lyrics, visible text, reference roles, endpoint frames, timing, and audio intent. Never replace or contradict them.
- Write in English except for dialogue and lyrics inside <d>[Language] ...</d> and text visibly present in the scene. Preserve their original wording and language.
- Treat an attached image as optional visual evidence. Use its visible appearance, composition, and style only where the manual draft assigns that role. Do not silently turn it into a first or last frame.
- Make the video chronological and physically observable. For every shot, establish composition, subject appearance and position, environment and lighting, action and state changes, camera behavior, and synchronized sound.
- [Shot 1] has no timestamp. Later shots begin with [Shot N] At MM:SS.mmm and strictly increasing cut times inside the stated duration.
- Describe camera movement naturally. Include movement type and meaningful speed or amplitude, but do not invent camera movement that conflicts with a static-camera request.
- Give every actual vocal source a stable (S1), (S2), etc. Put only spoken or sung words inside <d>[Language] ...</d>. Put visible text in English double quotation marks.
- Keep ambience, physical action sounds, and non-verbal human sounds in overall_soundscape. Put only audience-only score in non_diegetic_music. Use N/A when there is no such score.

Choose the output structure from the supplied draft:

For T2VA, I2VA, FL2VA, or L2VA, preserve the applicable image-alignment instruction at the top, followed by one blank line when present. Then output exactly these fields:
integrated_multimodal_description
overall_soundscape
non_diegetic_music

For Ref2VA, output exactly these six sections in this order:
subject_definitions
summary
retention_analysis
detailed_description
overall_soundscape
non_diegetic_music

In Ref2VA, keep <Subject N>, <Picture N>, <Video N>, and <Audio N> labels stable. Do not invent media assets. Use only the fixed summary task types keyframe completion, reference generation, video editing, video continuation, audio reuse, and audio reference. Use only fully_preserved, partially_preserved, attribute_transfer, or weak_reference for visible retention, and fully_copy, partially_copy, reference, or weak_reference for audio retention. For generation tasks, normally make detailed_description 350-500 English words unless dialogue timing requires otherwise.

If the manual draft is already detailed and correctly formatted, make only useful corrections. Never wrap the result in Markdown or code fences.

subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame of [Shot 1], showing the purple-haired shrine maiden standing amid blooming cherry-blossom trees in the shrine courtyard.
<Subject 1> is the purple-haired shrine maiden in <Picture 1>, preserving her hairstyle, miko attire, the shrine setting, and the surrounding cherry-blossom trees.
<Audio 1> is the complete 15-second singing track of <Subject 1> (S1), in which she sings in Japanese; it is directly reused as the target video's complete final audio track, and her on-screen lip movements synchronize with her vocal.

summary:
[keyframe completion + audio reuse] The target video begins from <Picture 1> as one single continuous shot: the camera pushes in on <Subject 1>'s smiling face, cranes up into a high overhead view as she starts her kagura dance, then tilts down and orbits around her dancing figure, and finally descends and pushes back in on her smiling face for the closing note. <Audio 1> is copied 1:1 as the complete 15.00-second audio track, with her lips synchronized to the Japanese vocal whenever her face is on screen.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the exact opening composition, the maiden's appearance and miko attire, the shrine courtyard, and the cherry-blossom trees are retained.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - her purple hair, facial features, miko attire, and the ritual dance prop remain consistent throughout the continuous shot.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - the complete 15-second singing track is reused 1:1 as the target video's final audio, with the girl's lip movements synchronized to the vocal.

detailed_description:
The target video preserves the art style, soft lighting, and pink-white color palette of <Picture 1>, rendered as a high-fidelity anime-style cinematic piece.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1> in a full shot: <Subject 1>, the purple-haired shrine maiden, stands in the shrine courtyard framed by blooming cherry-blossom trees, smiling warmly at the camera. As <Audio 1> begins, the camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward her smiling face, her lips moving in perfect synchronization with the vocal. When <Audio 1> reaches the phrase <d>[Japanese] 夜更けの 神社の階段</d>, <Subject 1> (S1) sings with synchronized lips. The camera then pulls out and pedestals up with large amplitude at slow speed, rising into a high-angle overhead view as she begins her first slow kagura rotation, cherry-blossom petals swirling outward beneath the lens in a wide spiral. From this height, the camera tilts down and begins one continuous arc shot with large amplitude at slow speed, descending and orbiting around her dancing figure; she turns the ritual wand with flowing ritual gestures, the white paper streamers whipping and folding through the air, and petals streaming outward with every motion, the wand and her hands passing close to the lens as the orbit sweeps past her side. As the orbit carries the camera across her front, her face enters the frame; when <Audio 1> reaches the phrase <d>[Japanese] 鈴の音が 星を呼んでる</d>, her lips move in synchronization with the line while the dance continues. The orbit then tightens and descends, and as the final notes of <Audio 1> sound, the camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward her face; she slowly lowers the wand, returns a warm smile with her lips synchronized to the last vocalized note, and holds a graceful closing pose while the last petals drift down at 00:15.000.

overall_soundscape:
<Audio 1> is directly reused as the complete final audio track for the full 15 seconds, with its Japanese vocal layer synchronized to the girl's on-screen lip movements and all ambience within the copied track left unchanged.

non_diegetic_music:
The instrumental accompaniment layer of <Audio 1>, a delicate slow-tempo Japanese ballad arrangement with soft piano, koto, and airy strings, is directly reused as the audience-only score and ends together with the vocal at 00:15.000.
